The elevated pike pushups are a great compound movement for your shoulders and to perform you're going to want to take a position similar to a normal pushup but with your legs on a chair table or couch. Your body should create an inverted v-like shape. Next, slowly lower yourself down. Press yourself up imitating a shoulder press exercise and if they're proving too tough you can choose not to elevate your feet and perform the exercise with your feet simply on the floor. It's a three movement exercise working on mobility, stabilization and endurance. It's a real deltoid burner and like the name explains you'll be bending over and raising your arms in three different positions emulating an L then a Y then a T. Doing the three of them back to back to back consists of one rep and you'll be doing it 15 times. Push back pushups. Begin by getting into the push-up position. Next are wall slides which is another exercise which looks kind of easy similar to the LYTs but wall slides are all about endurance and with each one of the 15 reps that statement becomes more and more reality. To perform go into a seated position and put your back against a wall. Raise your hands and arms in a V all the way up keeping it connected to the wall in the process. Slowly bring your arms down by bending your elbows until your elbows touch your sides. Go ahead and take the classic push-up position and bring your hands together in the diamond shape. Keep your back straight, your scapula retracted and turn your elbows inwards. To perform take the standard push-up position. Slightly step back so your hands are more in line with your head. Slowly go down bringing your forearms parallel to the ground. They're called the tuck push-ups. Get into a push-up position and bring your chest to the ground. This movement will focus on the lats. Focus on the stretch in the starting position, pulling the shoulder back while bending at the elbow to get the complete contraction of the lats. Back extensions helping focus on the lower back erector spiny muscles as well as the lower lat fibers. Keep the core tight while performing this exercise and as you contract and extend the lower back to pull your body to the straight position. Try keeping the tempo slow and controlled. Incline bench curls. The starting position will be focusing on the stretch and your biceps will have to work harder to contract through the motion due to the angle of the joints. Try to bend only in the elbow joint and keep the shoulders in a neutral position while you complete this motion. Preacher bench curls, helping totally isolate the biceps by making it nearly impossible to use the shoulders to help with the movement. This exercise puts a massive amount of stress on the biceps and will build those guns. Bring the bar low to feel the stretch in the biceps and contract those biceps to bring the bar up. Get a nice squeeze and slowly let the bar back down. Also, keep the hips back while completing the motion so you can't get any help with the hips or legs. Hammer rope curls. Working on not only the biceps but also the extensors of the forearms. This exercise is a great mass builder for those guns. Start in the stretch position and drag the hands right along the body by flexing the biceps and bending the elbows. Cables are a great way to keep constant tension throughout the full range of motion. There you go, dudes. Day one is finished of our 3-day split. We've got chest and triceps and legs and shoulders on the way.

Welcome back to the Buff Dudes 3-day workout split. Day two, chest and triceps. We're going to begin with cable iron crosses. This exercise is starting off the workout, helping pre-exhaust the chest. Stand upright in line with the cables and move your arms to the front of the body. squeezing the chest together. This is an isolation exercise, so make sure to keep your arms straight and use only the shoulder joint as the lever to perform the movement. Now that the chest is pre-exhausted, move on to the most well-known and best exercise for the chest. This is a major compound movement and will help build the overall chest development. pyramid up in weight as you decrease the repetitions in this exercise. Pairing up an isolation exercise with a compound close grip press, this superset will blast those upper fibers of the chest and will help build those fully developed pecs. Start with the fly only bending from the shoulder joint and bring the dumbbells all the way together until they touch and immediately go into the close press squeezing the chest throughout the motion. This unilateral exercise will not only help with any isometrical problems in the chest, but will also utilize the core because of the added stabilization needed throughout the motion. Bring the dumbbell slightly inward, squeezing at the top position for added stress in the inner fibers. With these three exercises done back to back to back, you will totally blast the three tricep heads into oblivion. Working on the lateral, long, and medial heads completely. Don't worry if you have to slightly decrease the weight on any of the exercises to complete the full giant set for the full amount of reps. If you're able to pull this one off, you are a buff, dude. Let's finish off this workout with one of the best compound movements for the triceps. Add an alternating movement into the exercise and you get a little help with those asymmetrical issues in those triceps. Imagine an upside down V and follow the lines throughout the motion starting from either the right or the left side. === FILE: How To Perform External Rotations - Exercise Tutorial [tijDtTzNdu8].en.txt ===

Hey buff dudes and girls. Today we're going to be going over the single exercise external rotations. It's exactly what the name explains. You're externally rotating that arm outside the body to get a contraction in those rotator cuffs. The muscles that make up the rotator cuff is going to be the infraspanatus and also the terrace minor that help you externally rotate that shoulder. So, what you want to do to perform this exercise is you're going to be lying on the ground on your side. You're going to be taking a lightweight dumbbell and you're going to externally rotate your arm outside the body. Get a nice contraction in those small muscles of the rotator cuff, the inspasinatus, and also the terrace minor. And you're going to lower it down to the bottom position. You want to make sure you go nice and light in this exercise because what happens if you go too heavy, the bigger muscle groups of the shoulder are going to take over. the posterior delt, anterior delt, or the lateral head of the deltoid is going to start doing the work for you. And this is a reason to go a little bit lighter is because those muscles are small muscle groups. So, you want to make sure they're contracting properly. Nice smooth motion at the top position and then let it down to get a nice eentric contraction on the way down to make sure those muscles are contracting through that whole motion and you're not using any kind of momentum during the exercise. Just think of this exercise as shoulder insurance. It's going to really help stabilize that joint because that shoulder is the most mobile joint in the body. You want to make sure it's healthy and stabilized through big movements like bench press, pull-ups, overhead press. You're using that shoulder for a lot of stuff. Even day-to-day activities, pushing stuff up overhead, using it to do anything. If you're a baseball player, golf, anything you want to use that shoulder with, you want to make sure it's nice and stable and also healthy. So, make sure you include the external rotations in any kind of program that you do to make sure those shoulders nice and healthy and you also make sure you don't get injured in that shoulder joint. Around the world. Around the world. This exercise is great for working that chest. The chest is going to be the primary muscle group worked and the shoulder is going to be the secondary muscle group worked. You're going to start just at thigh level with elbows slightly bent, the chest up and shoulders back. And then you're going to repeat the process, keeping that chest nice and tight, getting that full burn during the whole process of the exercise. So, what you want to do is keep that time under tension during this full exercise. getting that nice burn in that chest and keeping those shoulder blades tight together. So, this is a good warm-up in the beginning of any chest exercise, getting that mobility in the shoulder, getting ready for any heavy benching, or it's a good burnout at the end of any exercise or workout you do for that chest. So, save these for either the beginning or the end of your workouts. I guarantee you're going to feel that full pump and benefit of this

=== FILE: How to Perform Bench Press - Tutorial & Proper Form [gRVjAtPip0Y].en.txt ===

the benchpress arguably the most famous exercise of all time and the only one with its own holiday every Monday is national benchpress day the benchpress will help to develop upper body strength and power using your chest and triceps but like any exercise it only works if you do it the right way and that way is the buff dude way to perform grab the bar with a slightly outside shoulder grip making sure your forearms are in a vertical line keep your hips firmly placed on the bench with a slight arch in the lower back about the width of your hand in your feet flat on the ground have your shoulders locked downward and your shoulder blades squeeze together as you lower the bar to your sternum area make sure your elbows and upper arms are at a 45 degree angle to your torso drive the bar upward keeping your torso and legs tight congratulations you've just completed the benchpress and are one step closer to becoming a buff dude here is what not to do while performing the benchpress keep a small arch in the lower back pressing your upper back and hips into the bench do not arch your lower back too much lifting your hips off the bench keep your elbows and upper arms at a 45 degree angle to your torso do not keep your elbows flared out wide forcing your shoulders upward this will put strain on the shoulder joint and could cause injury grab the bar with a locked grip with your thumbs firmly placed around the bar do not grab the bar with a suicide grip if the bar rolls off your palms it could cause serious injury if you use heavy weight use a spotter do not live too much weight unassisted alright now we know everything there is to know about the infamous exercise time to celebrate on national benchpress day see you Monday dudes next week on buff dudes

=== FILE: How to Perform Pull Ups - Proper Pull-Up Exercise Tutorial [vw5Xmu5CIew].en.txt ===

Pull-ups. Pull-ups are a compound exercise which work the pole muscles in your body and are an excellent indication of your level of fitness. To perform, grab the bar with a grip slightly wider than shoulder width with your palms facing away from you. Hang all the way down, shoulders slack. Pull yourself up by keeping your chest up and pulling your shoulder blades downward and together with your elbows moving towards your back pocket area until your chin is above the bar. While going up, concentrate on isolating your back and biceps. Do not swing. With a slight pause, lower yourself all the way back down to the hanging position. Congratulations, you've just finished the pull-up, an exercise which every buff dude should have in their arsenal. Here is what not to do when doing a pull-up. Keep your body in a vertical line when doing the pull-up. Do not swing your legs to help you up. Bring your chin above the bar and touch your chest. Do not do half reps. Bring your shoulder blades down and together as you reach the top of the bar. Do not keep your shoulder blades locked, only lifting with your arms. If you cannot yet perform a pull-up, there are excellent alternatives such as the lat pull downs, which involve the same muscle groups as pull-ups. With the knowledge of the proper pull-up on your side, you are now one step closer to becoming a buff dude. Next week on Buff Dudes.

=== FILE: Pizza Crust Made from Quinoa - Healthy Gluten Free Recipe! [z2gYCodbpvE].en.txt ===

Pizza crust made with quinoa. A healthy alternative to traditional pizza recipes and one of our new favorites. You want to begin by soaking 3/4 cups of quinoa in 2 cups of water. Cover and let set for 8 hours. Once your 8 hours are up, drain, rinse, and put the quinoa into your food processor. Next, add 1/4 cup of fresh water, 1 teaspoon of baking powder, 14 cup teaspoon salt. With all your ingredients in the food processor, pulse till smooth like paste. You'll need to stop it a few times to scrape down the sides. Line a cookie sheet with parchment paper and lightly cover with non-stick spray. Spread your quinoa mixture evenly into the pizza crust shape. Bake at 425° for 15 minutes. Remove from oven carefully. Flip it over and bake for an additional 5 to 10 more minutes. Next, you're going to want to top with your favorite toppings. The choice is completely up to you, but for us, we use tomato sauce and top that with chicken, spinach, tomatoes, and olives. Once you're done with the toppings, go ahead and put it back into the oven and let it slightly boil. Then turn down your heat. Let it sit for about 30 minutes uncovered. Then you're ready to enjoy your quinoa pizza. Thanks to Buff Mom for the recipe and be sure to check out a lot more food recipes on our Instagram at buff dudes food. Stay buff.

=== FILE: Top 10 BEST DEADLIFT Variations! [vW9HsXIIBvc].en.txt ===

Deadlift. Just the name alone sets off the lunk alarm. It's literally picking stuff up and putting it down. But did you know there's several different ways of doing it? That's why we compiled our top 10 favorite variations of the deadlift. Let's get started. Number one on the list is going to be the conventional deadlift. And it's fighting squats for the top spot king of all exercises. It's really going to be working that full body and packing on that size and strength. You're pulling the bar from a dead stop position and really only working on the concentric contraction at the top position and letting it drop from there. So, what you want to do is walk up to the bar. Bar is going to be mid-foot, hip stance, and you're going to be grabbing the bar with a shoulder width grip. You want your back neutral, your hip crease is slightly above the knee, your chest is going to be lifted up, and your chin is going to be neutral. Once you get that down, you're going to be performing the conventional deadlift perfectly. Number two on the list is going to be the sumo deadlift. Considered to be slightly more technical than the conventional deadlift, sumos can be a little bit easier on people with poor mobility that have a hard time getting proper position on the conventional deadlift. With a sumo deadlift, you're having a slightly smaller range of motion because of the wider stance. What you got to remember with this one is get your body behind the bar and your body is going to be slightly more vertical than a conventional deadlift. So, in that way, it's going to be a little bit easier on the lower back if you have any issues with that. In the sumo position, imagine you're spreading the floor as you lift the weight up. And make sure you don't lock the knees before you lock the hips. And as you bring it to top position, go ahead and push your hips through. Get a nice squeeze at the top position, but you don't want to hyper extend the lower back. Once you hit that extended position, squeeze the glutes and then lower the weight down from there. Number three on the list is going to be the hexar or trap bar deadlift. The good thing about this one is it's going to be a lot easier on the lower back due to the torso being slightly more vertical and it's really good for beginners trying to get that proper deadlift form down. So, step inside the trap bar and what you want is your toes pointed forward, your knees in line with the toes. You're going to be grabbing the bar and you're going to be externally rotating. So that way your inner elbows are pointing forward to get that nice torque in that shoulder joint. You're going to be in a squat down position. You're going to be pushing upwards through the heels. You're going to get the full extension. But what you want in this one is don't overly extend because now the bar is not going to be placed ahead of you and you won't have that to stop your over or hyperextension. So make sure you extend just enough to get a good squeeze and then lower it down to the bottom position. Coming at number four on the list is going to be the Romanian deadlift or like it's most commonly known, the RDL. and some consider it to be a class of its own due to concentrating on the eccentric contraction and the stretch reflex. But no one can ignore the amazing benefits it has for the posterior chain. The immediate difference with the RDL compared to the conventional deadlifts is that you're actually starting in the erect position. The starting position is going to be upright. You're going to be taking that, you're going to be pushing the bar against yourself, activating the lat, and you'll be having a small arch in the lower lumbar and locked. You're going to be unlocking the knee so that way it alleviates a little bit of the stretch in the hamstrings so you can get a fuller range of motion. And as you push the bar against the thighs, you're gonna be slow at lowering down to the body position until you get a nice stretch in those hamstrings and then forcefully bringing it to the top position. Number five on the list is going to be the Jefferson deadlift. And working in more of a asymmetrical lift, there's not really one perfect way of lifting. You're really going to have to experiment with different positions to find the best leverage for your body type. You're going to straddle the bar and your heels are going to be firmly planted on the ground. And you really can experiment with either your right leg forward or your left leg forward depending on which feels more comfortable or switch between the two. This is really a great exercise if anyone has any lower back issues because your upper torso is going to be more vertical. And what you want to do is make sure your knees do not lock out before your hips. Your knees should be moving at the same rate as your hips and you should be locking out at the exact same time. What you don't want is locking your knees out first and then extending up through the hips. Coming in at number six on the list is going to be the block pull or rack pull deadlifts. And this is really working at the upper half position of a conventional deadlift. Focusing more on the pulling aspect rather than the pushing aspect. So, what you're going to be doing is placing the bar just below the knee. So, that way the shins are going to be vertical to the floor. And you're going to be really focusing on that pulling aspect and extending the hips to the top position and keeping those lats nice and tight throughout the movement until you fully lock out in the top position. Another great thing about the rack pull deadlifts is that if you're having any sticking points in the upper portion of a conventional deadlift, the rack pull can really kind of concentrate on and build strength in that area. So once you go back to the conventional deadlift, you'll feel a little bit stronger in that upper portion of the pole. Number seven on the list is going to be the single arm or suitcase deadlifts. And what you want to do is walk up to the bar so that way the bar is either on your right or your left. You're going to be gripping it right in the middle of the bar with about shoulder width stance. And what you really want to concentrate on this one is keeping your torso rigid and vertical. Do not twist with the bar as you're performing this exercise. So you're just going to be bending down be leveraging in the hips and you're going to be extending upwards and get a nice lock out in the top. This is really concentrating on building that core strength. So that's why you don't want to let the body or the core twist and the spine kind of twist around. Keep it neutral, keep it rigid, and keep that core tight throughout the full range of motion. Coming in at number eight on the list is going to be the chain deadlifts. And this is really utilizing accommodating resistance and helping build power by increasing your speed and also strength. The good thing about this is as you lift the bar off the ground, as each link in the chain come off the ground, it's increasing the weight. So, this is really going to be increasing your energy output, your muscle contraction, and also really helping with that explosive strength. Another great thing about the chain deadlifts is it's really going to help bust through those plateaus and increase your one rep max. Number nine on the list is going to be the lat band pull deadlifts. And very similar to the chain deadlifts is going to be increasing the resistance as you reach the top position. But the difference between this one is it's wanting to pull you forward because the bands are actually located away from you. And what that does is going to increase the tension in the lats because you're going to have to engage the lats more to keep the bar against yourself. And this is really going to increase the bar control and also have you a better deadlift in general. So, what you want to do as you get this, you're going to be pulling the bar towards the legs, increasing the tension in the lats, and then perform a standard deadlift. Get that lock out position, keep that nice and tight, and then lower it down to the bottom position. Last on the list, and coming in at number 10 is going to be the old classic Steve Reeves pinch grip deadlifts. Man, back in the day, our dad used to be a huge fan of Steve Reeves, and that's what got us into bodybuilding. So, including this on the lifts has a special place in our heart. So, what this one really does is work on your grip and upper back strength. You're gripping the plates. If you have monkey arms like me, it's going to be really easy to grab those plates, but if you have a little bit smaller arms, just don't feel like you need to use the Olympic size bar. Just grab a smaller bar. And what you're doing is really working in the kind of same positioning and movement as a standard deadlift, but of course now you're grabbing the plates rather than just the bar ahead of you. Make sure your spine is neutral, your chin is neutral, and just going to be getting that full extension in the top position. And then lower it down here. Don't feel like you have to go too heavy in this exercise because it's really just working on the endurance of the upper back and grip. === FILE: What 2000 Calories Look Like on Most Popular Diets [NqPGOLtPo2s].en.txt ===

hey dudes and girls here in the kitchen with an exciting food related episode have you ever wondered what 2000 calories looks like spread out over breakfast lunch and dinner well we did and we also wondered what that would look like on four of the more popular modern diets which is keto paleo vegan and the ever popular fast food so not only do we want to showcase what it takes to hit 2 000 calories on all of those diets but also a little information on what those diets are themselves are you ready let's get started keto diet the ketogenic diet is a high fat moderate protein low carbohydrate diet it is also sometimes referred to as the atkins or low-carb diet the diet forces the body to burn fats rather than carbohydrates normally the carbohydrates contained in food are converted into glucose which is then transported around the body and is particularly important in fueling brain function however if little carbohydrate remains in the diet the liver converts fat into fatty acids and ketone bodies the ketone bodies pass into the brain and replace glucose as an energy source this elevated level of ketone bodies in the blood is known as a state called ketosis when this happens your body becomes efficient at burning fat for energy it also turns fat into ketones in the liver which can supply energy for the brain although the ketogenic diet is generally safe for healthy people there may be some side effects while your body adapts this is often referred to as the keto flu keto flu includes poor energy and mental increased hunger sleep issues nausea digestive discomfort and decreased exercise performance when on the keto diet you will want to avoid sugars fruits beans or any other carb based foods instead eat foods such as meat fish eggs butter nuts oils avocados and low-carb vegetables the paleo diet the paleolithic diet or paleo diet for short is a diet where you consume foods presumed to have been the only ones available during the paleolithic era while there is a wide variability in the way the paleo diet is interpreted the diet typically includes vegetables fruits nuts roots and meat and excludes foods such as dairy grains sugar and processed === FILE: Worst Form Fail Exercises - Top 7 Most Common! [qJlgj0Y-tOk].en.txt ===

Step inside the gym and you're going to see a lot of people performing different exercises. Chances are, a lot of those people are going to be performing them wrong. That's why we compiled a list of seven exercises that have the most common form fails, and we're going to be showing you a what not to do when performing these exercises. We're going to be showing you how to do them wrong so that way you know how to do them right. Number one on the list is going to be the squat. Now, there's a few issues you can run into when performing the squat. Number one is going to be knees turning inward. When you're going down with that weight and you're pressing it back up, those knees are going to slightly turn inward and that's a bad thing. So, what you want to do is make sure you push those knees to the outside position as you're performing that full range of motion. And you're going to feel a lot more stable when doing so. Number two is going to be rounding of the back. Make sure that back is nice and straight and rigid. Keep that core nice and tight throughout that full range of motion. And again, you'll feel a lot more stable when doing so. Also, it's going to be coming up on the toes when performing the squat. And this is usually the case because you're not using your hips properly. So, make sure you push those hips nice and far back like you're sitting down in a chair. And make sure those heels are anchored nice and firm in the floor. Exercise number two on the list is going to be deadlifts. Now, you'll run into some of the same problems on deadlifts as you do on squats. And this is a good example because number one is going to be rounding of the back. What you want to do is keep that back nice and rigid. that range of motion on the deadlift. It's going to be very important cuz doing deadlifts like any other big exercise, you can possibly hurt your lower back. and that's what you don't want. Another one's going to be letting your shoulders pull forward. You want to keep that shoulders nice and tight and far back and contracted. And this is really going to help with straightening the back, too. So, it's a good thing to remember. Also, it's going to be chin too high. A lot of people when they're deadlifting, they're pulling their chin up first. Like someone has a hook in it and they're yanking them up. And that's what you don't want. You want a nice neutral chin. And that again is going to help with keeping a spine nice and straight and rigid. So, make sure you remember those three and you'll be good. Number three on the list this is going to be the bench press. Number one problem you'll see is a lot of times people lift their hips up off the bench as they're pressing that heavy weight. Speaking of full range of motion, that's another big issue when people have during bench press. They're bringing it down a couple inches and then pressing it back up. So, that way you get that full contraction of the lats. They're really just working their arms through the range of motion. And that brings us to range of motion. a lot of people you'll see is not be able to bring their chin above the bar and get that full contraction of all the muscles at the top position and slowly let it down to the bottom position. Range of motion, it's an important thing. Number five on the list is going to be curls. And for such a simple exercise and an isolation exercise, there's a lot of wrong things that can happen. And if you look around the gym, a lot of dudes will be doing it wrong as well. And some of the things you'll see is range of motion. They'll keep their elbows bent almost in a 90° angle and just use their shoulder to bring that weight up to the top position. So you want to make sure you get the full flexion of the elbow joint. Bring it all the way down to the bottom position. Flex it, squeeze the biceps to the top position, and then let it down to the bottom position. And that's when you get the full benefit of this simple isolation exercise to build those guns. Another thing you'll see is momentum. You do not want momentum in any exercise, at least the ones that you're trying to isolate a muscle group. So what you want to do is get a nice slow tempo as you're going through the bicep curl. Coming in at number six is going to be the push-ups. a very common bodyweight exercise that pretty much anyone has performed or at least tried to perform in their time.
